prompt.context: Your client, 6PAQ, is a small-market P.E. firm that specializes in suburban business development. One of its analysts identified two movie theaters in a small suburban area that separately or together might prove to be a good investment.
prompt.question: Should your client, 6PAQ, purchase these movie theaters?

clarifying_info.q: What is the condition of the theaters?
clarifying_info.a: The movie theaters are somewhat dilapidated.

clarifying_info.q: Is there competition in the area?
clarifying_info.a: None — they are the only two theaters in the suburb and surrounding suburbs.
Tickets (movies leased through distributors) and Concessions (purchased from distributors).
Suburban recreational facilities and entertainment: swimming pools, shopping malls, bowling alleys, laser tag facilities, etc.
100% ROI standard for all investments, sell in five years, and evaluate a potential modernization project.
From 2010–2018: ticket sales declined by 1.18%, but average ticket price increased by 15.46%.

exhibits.title: Revenue and Profitability by Theater
exhibits.shows: A time-series chart (2013–2018) plotting revenue and profitability lines for Theater A and Theater B separately.
exhibits.data: Theater A Revenue, Theater A Profitability, Theater B Revenue, Theater B Profitability — all tracked annually from 2013 to 2018.

framework: Financials — Revenue: Tickets (Price × Quantity) and Concessions (Price × Quantity)
Financials — Costs: Fixed costs (movie leases, labor, rent, taxes, electricity/HVAC, cleaning, insurance, maintenance) and Variable costs (concession costs)
Revenue Improvement Opportunities: marketing/customer analysis, price sensitivity, SKU analysis, gap analysis, advertising/discount spend
Entrance & Exit: purchase price, exit price, valuation methods (multiple, NPV, comparables), potential buyers
Other: synergies (bundle opportunities with portfolio companies, cross-sell), cost synergies (back-office, increased buying power)

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell you about the two theaters?
questions.guidance: Key insights: (1) Revenue has been consistent for both theaters and they have similar net profits. (2) Theater A has much higher revenue. (3) Theater A's costs are much higher as a percentage of revenue, indicating its cost structure could be improved.

questions.prompt: 6PAQ will send an analyst to each theater for a month to estimate the number of yearly visitors and revenue. The analyst cannot sit at the front or count customers directly. What instructions would you give and how would you calculate revenue?
questions.guidance: The candidate should derive a formula for total monthly visitors from screen count, seats per screen, fill capacity, and movies per screen per month. Then segment by ticket type (Premium vs Matinee) and concessions purchase rate. Key inputs to request: number of screens, seats per screen, average fill capacity, movies per screen per month, ticket price splits and prices, concession spend per customer and purchase rate.

math.setup: Tickets: # Screens × Seats/Screen × Avg Fill Capacity × Movies/Screen/Month = Total Monthly Visitors. Then multiply by % Premium (or Matinee), ticket price, and 12 months. Concessions: Monthly Visitors × Avg Spend × % Who Buy × 12 months.
steps: Theater A Visitors: 10 screens × 80 seats × 75% fill × 20 movies/screen/month = 12,000/month
Theater B Visitors: 10 screens × 80 seats × 50% fill × 20 movies/screen/month = 8,000/month

questions.prompt: Total costs are: Theater A = 50% of revenue, Theater B = 20% of revenue. What could be driving the cost difference, and what is each theater's profitability?
questions.guidance: Possible cost drivers for Theater A's higher cost ratio: higher electricity/HVAC costs, movie lease structure, rent on larger property, unionized labor, poor distributor relationships, SKU choices. Candidate should brainstorm these buckets before calculating.

math.answer: Theater A profit: ~$1m; Theater B profit: ~$1.1m; Combined: ~$2.1m

questions.prompt: The analyst proposes a modernization project: install arcades, nicer seats, a new mobile app, and an HVAC system for Theater A — costing $4m upfront. After 1 year of development (theaters operate as-is during that year), both theaters will generate 50% additional revenue and Theater A's cost ratio will drop to Theater B's level (20%). Should 6PAQ undergo this project, consistent with its 100% ROI criterion?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate recognizes: Year 1 is the construction year (no improvement to profit), so the incremental profit window is Years 2–5 (4 years). They should compute new revenues, new costs, new net income, then incremental net income over 4 years, and divide by the $4m investment.

math.setup: Incremental Profit = (New Annual NI − Current Annual NI) × 4 years; ROI = (Incremental Profit − Investment) / Investment
math.answer: Modernization ROI = 100%, exactly meeting the 100% hurdle rate.

questions.prompt: The purchase price multiple is 5× Net Income and the exit price multiple is 6× post-modernization Net Income. Does the overall investment clear 6PAQ's 100% ROI hurdle?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate notes that exit NI is the post-modernization figure ($4.06m) and that purchase NI is the current figure ($2.1m). The overall ROI of ~132% exceeds the 100% hurdle. They should also note that the expansion of multiple (5× to 6×) contributes meaningfully.

math.setup: Purchase Price = Current NI × 5; Exit Price = New NI × 6; ROI = (Exit Price − Purchase Price) / Purchase Price
math.answer: Overall investment ROI ≈ 132%, exceeding the 100% hurdle.

brainstorming.prompt: What are ways 6PAQ could improve revenues at these theaters?

categories.name: New Products / Existing Customers
ideas: Charge for parking if lot is owned
Introduce new food or alcohol offerings

categories.name: Existing Products / New Customers
ideas: Offer other types of entertainment (local plays)
Offer theme nights or diversify targeted movies (cult classics reruns)

categories.name: New Products / New Customers
ideas: Cross-sell to customers of other portfolio companies

categories.name: Cost Drivers (Theater A higher cost ratio)

recommendation: 6PAQ should invest in both theaters and undertake the modernization project.
With new improvements and monopoly pricing power, it can achieve over 100% ROI on both the modernization project and the overall theater investment.
Modernization project ROI = 100%; overall theater investment ROI ≈ 132%, both clearing the 100% hurdle.
risks: Substitutes and threats: new local entrants; Netflix and streaming services eroding demand.

Accuracy of assumptions: NI multiple increase (5× to 6×) may not materialize; improved NI from investment may be overstated; no discount rate or opportunity cost applied — 100% ROI on modernization leaves little margin for error.
Theater owners may not be willing to sell.
next_steps: Conduct intelligence gathering using 6PAQ's existing industry relationships; purchase market research reports to assess threat timelines.
Further analyze and triangulate all financial assumptions.
Approach theater owners to gauge interest and initiate acquisition discussions.
